title: Refactor health telemetry pipeline for graceful load shedding and cross-region failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Recent region-level incidents revealed that our current readiness/liveness probe signals are too binary and noisy for autoscaler decisioning. This leads to oscillation in Dedicated pools and poor SLO adherence under partial regional overloads. Objective: Refactor the health telemetry pipeline to emit graded health scores (0-100) per-serving-unit, introduce a distributed health aggregator that computes robust percentile-based readiness, and wire those signals into: 1) circuit-breaker gating for cross-region failover, 2) autoscaler hysteresis and derating policies, and 3) load-shedding policies for graceful degradation.
acceptance_criteria: Health signal aggregator produces per-region P50/P95/P99 latency and error-rate summaries at 15s and 1m windows
Readiness now depends on a smoothed health score (EWMA alpha=0.2) and a minimum P95 tail latency threshold
Autoscaler uses derated capacity when region health < 60 for >30s; oscillation tests show reduced bounce (less than 10% scale up/down churn over synthetic spike)
Circuit breaker triggers failover after two consecutive 15s windows where health score < 40, and supports manual forced-open for incident response
Load-shedding policy drops low-priority requests first and preserves stateful/enterprise traffic; SLO impact tracked and limited to planned degradation budget
success_metrics: Reduce autoscaler-induced p95 latency spikes during multi-region spillovers by >= 40%
Decrease scale churn (scale events per 5m) by >= 60% under synthetic step-load tests
Maintain 99.9% availability for P1 customer traffic during simulated single-region failure with cross-region failover enabled
design_decisions: Move health score calculation out of each node and into a sidecar + aggregator to avoid duplicated state
Use EWMA for short-term smoothing and a percentile store (approx quantiles) for tail estimation to avoid being poisoned by outliers

Implement graded readiness with three bands: Healthy (>70), Degraded (40-70), Unhealthy (<40). Only Healthy nodes are considered for steady-state traffic, Degraded nodes are used for best-effort/cached responses, Unhealthy nodes are drained and circuit-breaker counted
Autoscaler integration uses gated metrics: only counts Healthy capacity fully, Degraded capacity at 30% effective weight
Circuit breaker policy ties into regional routing: once a region enters Unhealthy, gradual traffic reroute to warm standby with 10s ramp per instance to avoid cold shock
implementation_notes: Plan: 1) Small refactor to emit per-request health measurements (latency, error flags, backend queue). 2) Sidecar collects and ships to a region-local aggregator (gRPC stream). 3) Aggregator computes percentiles and publishes health scores to the control plane and metrics (Prometheus). 4) Autoscaler and routing components subscribe to health topics. We will reuse existing kernel for quantile approximation (t-digest) from infra-lib. Backwards compatibility: fall back to current binary probes if aggregator unavailable.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Added aggregation path increases control-plane load. Mitigation: sample at 1/10th for non-P0 routes and use sketch-based summaries.

Risk: New heuristics might surprise existing customers. Mitigation: feature-flag rollout, default disabled for accounts with dedicated SLA unless opted-in; add explicit release notes and migration playbook.
Risk: Incorrect derate weights could reduce effective capacity. Mitigation: conservative defaults, controlled canary with synthetic traffic and canary dashboards
rollout_plan: - Stage 1 (canary region): Deploy sidecar + aggregator in staging and one low-traffic region; enable health-score export only to internal dashboards. Run synthetic spike tests (GH PR: runtime#3201). - Stage 2 (opt-in customers): Enable feature flag for small set of Dedicated customers and monitor canary dashboards for 48h. - Stage 3 (gradual global): Enable for all regions with 5% traffic ramp per 30 minutes and automatic rollback conditions (error-rate > 2x baseline or scaling churn > 15% above expected).
rollback_plan: Flip feature flag off at control-plane; aggregator fallback to binary probes; automate route rebalancing to pre-flag weights. Run incident postmortem if rollback triggered.
metrics_and_dashboards: Dashboards to add: Region Health Score (P50/P95/P99), Autoscaler effective capacity vs nominal, Scale churn chart, Circuit-breaker open count per region, Shed rate by priority. Alert rules: Health score < 40 for 2 consecutive windows -> P1; scale churn > threshold -> P2. Link to dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/health-agg/health-telemetry
